<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout-note" markdown="1">
**Updated 29 December 2020**: All these pieces of work are already available

function. Just install it via `install.packages("cartography")`. A dedicated

</div>

Want to use a flag (or any `*.png` file) as a background for your map? You are
in the right place. I am aware that there are some **R** packages out
[there](https://github.com/RobertMyles/flagfillr), but we focus here on the
option provided by `cartography::getPngLayer()`, which basically converts your
image into a raster. See also Paul Murrell's article **"Raster Images in R
Graphics"** [(_The **R** Journal, Volume 3/1, June 2011_)](https://journal.r-project.org/archive/2011/RJ-2011-008/RJ-2011-008.pdf).


## Required **R** packages

```{r}
#| label: libs
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-cap: ""
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(cartography)
library(mapSpain)
library(giscoR)
```

## Choosing a good source for our shape

In this post, I am going to plot a map of Spain with its
[autonomous communities (plus 2 autonomous cities)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_communities_of_Spain),
which are the first-level administrative divisions of the country.
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_communities_of_Spain)
shows an initial map that also identifies the flag of each territory.

For that, I will use **mapSpain**, which uses information from **giscoR**, whose
source is the geodata available in [**Eurostat**](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat).
I will also use **giscoR** to get the world around Spain.


```{r}
#| label: 20190618_preparing
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
#| fig-height: !expr 550/90
#| fig-width: !expr 750/90
#| paged-print: false
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Map of Spain with autonomous community boundaries and a separate box for the Canary Islands."
Spain <- esp_get_ccaa(epsg = 3857, res = 3)

World <- gisco_get_countries(epsg = 3857, res = 3)

bboxcan <- esp_get_can_box(epsg = 3857)

# Plot
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(st_geometry(Spain),
  col = NA,
  border = NA,
  bg = "#C6ECFF"
)
plot(st_geometry(World),
  col = "#E0E0E0",
  bg = "#C6ECFF",
  add = T
)
plot(st_geometry(Spain), col = "#FEFEE9", add = T)
layoutLayer(
  title = "",
  frame = FALSE,
  scale = 500,
  sources = gisco_attributions(),
  author = "dieghernan, 2019",
)
plot(bboxcan, add = TRUE)
```



Now we have it! A nice map of Spain with a layout based on the [Wikipedia convention for location maps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Maps/Conventions/Location_maps).

## Loading the flag

As a first example, I chose [Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asturias)
to build my code. The goal here is to create a `RasterBrick` from the desired
`*.png` file, add the necessary geographical information and use the shape of
Asturias to crop the flag.

```{r}
#| label: 20190618_Asturias
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tidy: styler
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: !expr 1000/90
#| fig-height: !expr (500/2)/90
#| paged-print: false
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Two maps comparing the rectangular flag of Asturias with the same flag clipped to the boundary of Asturias."
# 1.Shape---
shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Asturias")

# 2.Get flag---

# Masked
url <- "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Flag_of_Asturias.svg/800px-Flag_of_Asturias.svg.png"

flagnomask <- getPngLayer(shp, url, mask = FALSE)

flagmask <- getPngLayer(shp, url, mask = TRUE)

opar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1), mfrow = c(1, 2))
pngLayer(flagnomask)
plot(st_geometry(Spain), add = T)

# 4.Mask---
pngLayer(flagmask)
plot(st_geometry(Spain), add = T)
par(opar)
```



<div role="note" aria-label="Tip" class="callout-tip" markdown="1">
Use high-quality `*.png` files,
otherwise the plot will look quite poor. Here I show an extreme example.
</div>

```{r}
#| label: 20190618_svg
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tidy: styler
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: !expr 800/(90)
#| fig-height: !expr 550/(90)
#| paged-print: false
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Two flag-filled maps of Murcia comparing low and high image resolutions. The higher-resolution flag has smoother edges."
MURshp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Murcia")
MURLow <- getPngLayer(
  MURshp,
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Flag_of_the_Region_of_Murcia.svg/100px-Flag_of_the_Region_of_Murcia.svg.png"
)
MURHigh <- getPngLayer(
  MURshp,
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Flag_of_the_Region_of_Murcia.svg/1200px-Flag_of_the_Region_of_Murcia.svg.png"
)


# Plot and compare
opar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
plot_sf(MURshp, main = "Low")
pngLayer(MURLow, add = TRUE)

plot_sf(MURshp, main = "High")
pngLayer(MURHigh, add = TRUE)

par(opar)
```

```{r}
#| label: 20190618_finalmap
#| tidy: styler
#| eval: false
#| fig-cap: ""
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mfrow = c(1, 1))
plot(
  Spain %>%
    st_geometry(),
  col = NA,
  border = NA,
  bg = "#C6ECFF"
)
plot(st_geometry(World),
  col = "#E0E0E0",
  add = T
)
plot(st_geometry(bboxcan),
  add = T
)
layoutLayer(
  title = "",
  frame = FALSE,
  sources = "© EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries",
  author = "dieghernan, 2019",
)
# Andalucia
flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Bandera_de_Andalucia.svg/1000px-Bandera_de_Andalucia.svg.png"
shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Andalucía")
pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag), add = TRUE)

# ...more flags
# Go to the source code of this post on GitHub for the full code

plot(st_geometry(Spain),
  col = NA,
  lwd = 2,
  add = T
)
```

```{r}
#| label: 20190618_allCCAA
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: !expr 550/90
#| fig-width: !expr 750/90
#| paged-print: false
#| fig-dpi: 90

#| fig-alt: "Map of Spain with each autonomous community filled with its flag and the Canary Islands shown in an inset."
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mfrow = c(1, 1))
plot(
  Spain %>%
    st_geometry(),
  col = NA,
  border = NA,
  bg = "#C6ECFF"
)
plot(st_geometry(World),
  col = "#E0E0E0",
  add = T
)
plot(st_geometry(bboxcan),
  add = T
)
layoutLayer(
  title = "",
  frame = FALSE,
  sources = "© EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries",

# Andalucia
flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Bandera_de_Andalucia.svg/1000px-Bandera_de_Andalucia.svg.png"
shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Andalucía")
pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag), add = TRUE)


# Aragon
flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Flag_of_Aragon.svg/1200px-Flag_of_Aragon.svg.png"
shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Aragón")
pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag, align = "left"), add = TRUE)

# Asturias
flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Flag_of_Asturias.svg/1200px-Flag_of_Asturias.svg.png"
shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Asturias")
pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag), add = TRUE)

pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag), add = TRUE)

# Castilla y León

shp <- Spain %>% filter(iso2.ccaa.code == "ES-CL")

shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Madrid")
pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag), add = TRUE)

flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Bandera_de_Navarra.svg/1200px-Bandera_de_Navarra.svg.png"
shp <- Spain %>% filter(ccaa.shortname.es == "Navarra")
pngLayer(getPngLayer(shp, flag), add = TRUE)

# Comunidad Valenciana
flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Flag_of_the_Land_of_Valencia_%28official%29.svg/1200px-Flag_of_the_Land_of_Valencia_%28official%29.svg.png"
shp <- Spain %>% filter(iso2.ccaa.code == "ES-VC")

# Extremadura
flag <-
  "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Flag_of_Extremadura_%28with_coat_of_arms%29.svg/1200px-Flag_of_Extremadura_%28with_coat_of_arms%29.svg.png"

# Baleares

# La Rioja

flag <-

shp <- Spain %>% filter(iso2.ccaa.code == "ES-RI")

# Basque Country

flag <-

shp <- Spain %>% filter(iso2.ccaa.code == "ES-PV")

plot(st_geometry(Spain),
```

We are done now. If you have suggestions, you can leave a comment. As always,
if you enjoyed the post, you can share it on your preferred social network.

```{r}
#| label: 20190618_imgpost
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: !expr 533/90
#| fig-width: !expr 800/90
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Map of Europe in dark blue with a ring of yellow European Union stars on a light blue background."
nuts1 <- gisco_get_nuts(nuts_level = "1", epsg = 3035, res = 3)


noplot <- c("FRY", "ES7", "PT2", "PT3")
NUTS1_Clean <- nuts1 %>%
  filter(CNTR_CODE %in% eurostat::eu_countries$code) %>%
  filter(!NUTS_ID %in% noplot) %>%
  group_by(CNTR_CODE) %>%
  summarise(drop = n())

url <- "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Flag_of_Europe.svg/1200px-Flag_of_Europe.svg.png"

flag <- getPngLayer(NUTS1_Clean, url, mask = FALSE)
flagcut <- getPngLayer(NUTS1_Clean, url, mask = TRUE)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
pngLayer(flag, alpha = 150)
pngLayer(flagcut, bgalpha = 0, add = T)
```
